- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to underreact — adjust forecast upward by 1–3% relative to recent mean.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overcorrects downward — reduce forecast slope by 0.5–1.5% per day post-spike.
- If supply net is strongly bearish (net < -15) and sentiment is neutral or bearish, model underestimates downside — add 2–5% downward bias to forecast mean.
- In high-event periods (≥20 events/30d), model tends to overestimate short-term volatility — smooth forecast curve by reducing daily increments by 0.2–0.5%.
- When sentiment flips from bullish to bearish (e.g., -0.5 to 0.0), model often lags — adjust forecast to reflect 1–2 day lag in reversal, with 10–20% downward shift on day 2.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture mean reversion after 3–5 consecutive days above 75 — apply downward correction of 1–3% per day until price stabilizes.
